goal: A runner step is not killed, failed or re-dispatched by mc's own bookkeeping: a machine sleep, a resumed session's zero-turn result, a branch whose PR already merged, and a step that has landed each lead to the right state without a person.
Lane slots are counted truthfully: a dead runner's lane file is swept, and the total cap is read live and holds across every live runner.
A session started outside a repository is held by that repository's PreToolUse safety hooks, and the daily digest stops counting landings as failures.
contract: No step changes how the merger measures or lands a pull request.
The register stays the one place a step's state lives (ruling 21); no step writes plan state into PLAN.json except `met` in the last step.
The repositories' hook scripts are run as they are, never copied into mc.
Every existing `mc run`, `mc step` and `mc hook` behaviour not named in a step stays as it is.
out_of_scope: Resuming a session that was already killed `stalled` on the machine-restart path, and fault 4 committing a `failed` step's leftovers. With the guard fixed, a sleep no longer produces that kill.
Holding a `caffeinate -i` assertion while a lane runs. A battery at 1 % forces sleep anyway.
Repairing the register rows of feed-topics step 4, sql-postgres-plans step 1 and msr-core-finish-measure step 1. These were readied by hand already.
The stall guard for codex sessions, which have none (`watchFor` returns `{}`).
`push-guard.js` and `mc publish`'s merged-branch refusal: unchanged. They now meet a branch the runner has already moved.
`plan-branch.js` and `work-area.js` (`releaseVerdict`) still use `mergedPullAtTip` alone. Any change there is a separate question.

Unblocking a step when a plan pull request answers its decision. The runner does not read decisions, by Martin's word of 2026-08-29 (quoted in `chooseKind`'s comment, `src/mc/run-plan.js`). The step comes back with `mc step ready`, run by whoever applied the answer.
`per_repo` taking effect in a running runner (lane loops exiting or being spawned when it changes): it still takes `mc run --update`, and the verb says so.
The page (`nowBlock`, `src/mc/status-collect.js`) sweeping files: it stays a pure reader and keeps drawing `stale:` until a runner sweeps.
A dead pid reused by an unrelated process, which `pidAlive` reads as alive.
An ordering rule between lanes waiting for a slot.

PostToolUse hooks of a repository (memoro's `post-push-todo.sh`, `check-wrangler-on-push.sh`) for a session started outside it: only PreToolUse blocks, and the global registration has no PostToolUse entry for mc.
Codex plan sessions (`mc plan --codex`): Codex reads no Claude Code hooks.
Launching plan sessions inside a checkout, or with `--settings`: rejected in step 1 in favour of mc's global pre-tool hook.

Dropping the project name from runner fingerprints (the proposal's second suggestion): `signature` keeps `{ name }` on purpose (2026-09-06), and with landings no longer counted a repeat failure per project is a real line.
Notes like `success,failed` and `success,blocked` with exit 0, which the `/success/` test also skips: a separate question.
The causes of `mc failed: gate exited N` and `shot exited N` in the digest.
memoro's missing `scripts/admin/inspect-*` script for the messaging send log (a memoro proposal).

steps.title: The stall guard re-arms across a machine sleep instead of killing
steps.done_when: `streamSession` in `src/mc/run.js` runs a 30-second heartbeat beside the stall timer, re-arms the guard and calls `onSleep(minutes)` when a gap over three minutes fell inside the silence; the two new tests in `tests/mc/run-session.test.js` and the new assertion in `tests/mc/run.test.js` pass; `mc gate` is green.
instruction: Why: on 2026-10-17 the Mac slept from 08:55:38Z to 09:21:22Z (`pmset -g log`: 'Low Power Sleep' at 1 % battery). feed-topics step 4 and sql-postgres-plans step 1 were both killed `stalled` (rc 142), at 09:22:45Z and 09:22:41Z, which is a minute after the wake. feed-topics had made a tool call at 08:55:35Z and was close to done. The stall guard is `armStall` in `streamSession` (`src/mc/run.js` lines 342–357), a `setTimeout(stallMs)` re-armed on every stdout chunk (`scan`, line 383). Nothing on that path knows the machine slept. Node's timer clock counts sleep on this Mac. Measured on 2026-10-18 with Node v24.10.0 and libuv 1.51.0: `process.hrtime` is within 9 s of wall-clock time since boot, across at least 15 minutes of sleep since boot. So a stall timer comes due during sleep and fires as soon as the machine wakes.

The design is a heartbeat that notices gaps between its ticks. Comparing wall-clock time with monotonic time (`Date.now()` against `performance.now()` or `process.hrtime`) does not work here: both clocks advance during sleep on this machine, so there is no difference to see. A `setInterval` that records `Date.now()` every 30 s works whichever clock libuv uses. If timers count sleep, the overdue tick fires at wake and sees the whole sleep as one gap. If they do not, the next tick after wake sees it. The trap: when timers count sleep, every overdue timer fires at wake in order of due time, so the stall timer can fire before the heartbeat tick that would have seen the gap. The stall callback must therefore run the gap check itself before it decides anything.

In `src/mc/run.js`, below `TOTAL_POLL_MS` (line 236), add two exported constants with a one-line doc comment each: `export const SLEEP_TICK_MS = 30 * 1000;` (how often a session's heartbeat looks at the wall clock) and `export const SLEEP_GAP_MS = 3 * 60 * 1000;` (a gap between two heartbeats longer than this means the runner did not run: the machine slept). The gap is three minutes so that a synchronous `sh()` call, whose timeout is 120 s (line 240), is never taken for a sleep.

In `streamSession` (line 288), add the option `onSleep = null` after `onQuiet = null`. After `let asked = false;` (line 336) add: `let lastBeat = Date.now(); let slept = 0; let beatTimer = null;` and `const beat = () => { const now = Date.now(); const gap = now - lastBeat; lastBeat = now; if (gap > SLEEP_GAP_MS) slept += gap - SLEEP_TICK_MS; };`. Add `clearInterval(beatTimer);` to `stop` (line 337). In the `setTimeout` callback inside `armStall`, right after `if (settled) return;`, add: `beat(); if (slept > 0) { const minutes = Math.round(slept / 60_000); slept = 0; try { onSleep?.(minutes); } catch { /* a log line, not the session */ } armStall(); return; }`. The existing background-task and kill code follows unchanged. In `scan`, after `asked = false;` (line 382), add `slept = 0;`, because a chunk shows the session is alive and the guard re-arms from it. Just before the final `armStall();` (line 413), add `if (stallMs) beatTimer = setInterval(beat, SLEEP_TICK_MS);`. Use no other clock: the tests drive `Date` through `mock.timers`.

In the doc comment above `streamSession` (lines 245–287), after the sentence that ends 'is killed at the next `stallMs`.', add: 'A machine that slept is not a silent session: a heartbeat every `SLEEP_TICK_MS` reads the wall clock, and when the guard fires with a gap over `SLEEP_GAP_MS` inside the silence (the stall timer can be the first to wake, so it looks too), it calls `onSleep(minutes)` and re-arms for a full `stallMs` instead of killing.'
In `watchFor` in `src/mc/run.js` (line 1276), next to `onQuiet`, add `onSleep: (minutes) => { say(`${name}: machine slept ${minutes} min — stall guard re-armed`); },`.

Tests in `tests/mc/run-session.test.js`, inside `describe('streamSession')`, using the existing `start`, `run` and `MINUTE` helpers and the fake timers set up in `beforeEach` (`setTimeout`, `setInterval`, `Date`, now 0). `mock.timers.setTime(t)` moves the mocked `Date` without running timers, and the next `tick` fires every timer then due, in order of due time, with `Date.now()` at the moment after the tick. That is how a wake looks when timers count sleep. (1) 're-arms the stall guard across a machine sleep instead of killing, and says how long it slept': `const slept = []; const { child, session } = start({ onSleep: (m) => slept.push(m) }); run(child, 5); mock.timers.setTime(Date.now() + 26 * MINUTE); mock.timers.tick(1);` then `child.killed` deepEquals `[]` and `slept` deepEquals `[26]`; `run(child, 19)` leaves `killed` `[]`; `run(child, 1)` makes it `['SIGTERM']`; and `(await session).stalled` is true. (2) 'sees the sleep when the stall timer is the first to wake': `start({ onSleep })` the same way; `mock.timers.tick(10_000); child.say(JSON.stringify({ type: 'assistant', message: { content: [] } })); run(child, 19); mock.timers.tick(55_000);` and `killed` is `[]` (the stall is due at 20 min 10 s, and the last heartbeat ran at 20 min 0 s); then `mock.timers.setTime(Date.now() + 26 * MINUTE); mock.timers.tick(1);` and `killed` is `[]` and `slept` is `[26]`. This test fails if `beat()` is left out of the stall callback, so keep both. Every existing test in the file passes unchanged: `run()` ticks one minute at a time, which stays well under `SLEEP_GAP_MS`.

In `tests/mc/run.test.js`, in the test 'one step: worktree made from origin/main, session through the adapter, PR merged, row logged' (line 688), after the `call.checkIn(60, 1)` assertion (line 702) and the runner.log match after it, add `call.onSleep(26);` and `assert.match(f.files['/w/runner/log/runner.log'], /alpha: machine slept 26 min — stall guard re-armed/u);`.

In `docs/technical/mc-run.md`, at the end of the paragraph that begins 'A session waiting on a background task is silent' (ends line 1156), add one paragraph: on 2026-10-17 two live sessions were killed `stalled` a minute after the Mac woke from a 26-minute sleep, because Node's timer clock counts sleep on macOS and the stall timer came due while the machine slept. Since then a heartbeat every 30 s (`SLEEP_TICK_MS`) reads the wall clock, a gap over three minutes (`SLEEP_GAP_MS`) between ticks is a sleep, and a guard that fires with a sleep inside its silence re-arms for a full `stall_minutes` with the line `<name>: machine slept <n> min — stall guard re-armed` in `runner.log`.
`mc gate tests/mc/run-session.test.js tests/mc/run.test.js`, then `mc gate`, `mc publish`, `mc merge memoro-cli <pr>`.

steps.title: A resumed session's zero-turn task-notification result is not its end
steps.done_when: `scan` in `streamSession` (`src/mc/run.js`) and `sessionResult` (`src/mc/run-plan.js`) skip a `result` line whose `num_turns` is 0; the two new tests in `tests/mc/run-session.test.js` and the new test in `tests/mc/run-plan.test.js` pass; `mc gate` is green.
instruction: Why: on 2026-10-17 at 20:25Z the runner resumed msr-core-finish-measure step 1 (session f266c900…), cold. The stream (`~/mc/runner/log/msr-core-finish-measure-20261017T202540Z.jsonl`) starts with `hook_started`, `hook_response`, then `{"type":"system","subtype":"task_notification","task_id":"b0sv52dnz","status":"stopped","summary":"Background shell command didn't finish before the previous session ended",…}`, then `init`. Its fifth line is `{"type":"result","subtype":"success","is_error":false,"num_turns":0,"duration_api_ms":0,"result":"","origin":{"kind":"task-notification"},…}`. `scan` in `streamSession` (`src/mc/run.js` line 394) takes any `result` line with no background task alive as the end: it ends stdin and starts the two-minute result grace. The session went on working. The grace killed it ('did not exit within 2m of its result — killed, the result stands'), and the step was failed 'success (rc 0) with no pull request'.

What tells this line apart is `num_turns: 0`, not `origin.kind`. Across all 139 stream logs in `~/mc/runner/log/` on 2026-10-18, 29 result lines carry `origin.kind: "task-notification"`. 28 of them are real turn ends: claude starting a turn by itself when a background task finished, with `producer: "session-task"`, a `runId` and `num_turns` ≥ 1. Eleven of those are the session's last line. This stale line is the only result with `num_turns: 0`. Results whose text is an API error have `num_turns: 1`, `duration_api_ms: 0` and are real ends. So filtering on `origin.kind` would hang every session whose last turn followed a background task. Filter on `num_turns === 0`, and treat a missing `num_turns` as a turn: the `RESULT_LATE` fixture has none.

In `src/mc/run.js`, `scan` (line 394): change the condition to `else if (event?.type === 'result' && !tasks.length && event.num_turns !== 0) { onResultLine(); return; }`. Put a comment above it: a resumed session whose background shell died with the previous process opens with a `task_notification` and a `result` of zero turns (`origin.kind: task-notification`), which answers nothing, and taking it for the end killed msr-core-finish-measure on 2026-10-17. A task-notification result with turns is a real end.

In `src/mc/run-plan.js`, `sessionResult` (lines 1267–1288): push only results with `event.num_turns !== 0` (line 1273). In the whole-JSON fallback (line 1278), also return null when `json.type === 'result' && json.num_turns === 0`. Add one sentence to its doc comment: a zero-turn `result` (the stale notification a resume opens with) is no answer and is skipped. As a result, a stream whose only result is that line reads as no result: `writeSessionLogs` falls back to `streamSummary`, `readSessionOutput` says `no-json`, and a session killed by a signal goes down the interrupted path at `src/mc/run.js` line 2725 instead of being counted as having answered.

Tests in `tests/mc/run-session.test.js`, inside `describe('streamSession')`, with the existing `start`, `RESULT` and `MINUTE`: (1) 'does not take the stale task-notification result a resume starts with for the end': `child.say(JSON.stringify({ type: 'system', subtype: 'task_notification', task_id: 'b0sv52dnz', status: 'stopped', summary: "Background shell command didn't finish before the previous session ended", session_id: 'sid' }))`, then `child.say(JSON.stringify({ type: 'result', subtype: 'success', is_error: false, num_turns: 0, duration_api_ms: 0, result: '', origin: { kind: 'task-notification' }, session_id: 'sid' }))`; `child.stdin.ended` is false; after `mock.timers.tick(3 * MINUTE)`, `child.killed` is `[]` (no grace was armed); after `child.say(RESULT)`, `child.stdin.ended` is true. (2) 'takes a task-notification result with turns for the end': `child.say(JSON.stringify({ type: 'result', subtype: 'success', num_turns: 3, origin: { kind: 'task-notification', producer: 'session-task', runId: 'r1' }, session_id: 'sid' }))` and `child.stdin.ended` is true.

In `tests/mc/run-plan.test.js`, inside `describe('readSessionOutput on a stream-json run')` (line 640), using its `init`, `assistant` and `result` fixtures: 'a zero-turn task-notification result is no answer': `const stale = result({ num_turns: 0, duration_api_ms: 0, result: '', origin: { kind: 'task-notification' } });`. Then `sessionResult([init, stale, assistant].join('
'))` is null; `readSessionOutput({ toolId: 'claude-code', stdout: [init, stale, assistant].join('
'), exitCode: 143 }).note` is `'no-json'`; and `sessionResult([init, stale, assistant, result()].join('
'))` has `num_turns` 4 and `result` `'done'`.

In `docs/technical/mc-run.md`, at the end of the paragraph that begins 'A `result` is not the end while a **background task** runs' (ends line 1129), add: nor is a `result` of zero turns. A resumed session whose background shell died with the previous process opens with a `task_notification` and a `result` with `num_turns: 0` and `origin.kind: task-notification`. On 2026-10-17 the runner took that for the end and killed msr-core-finish-measure two minutes into its resume. The scan and `sessionResult` skip it. A task-notification result with turns, which is claude's own next turn after a background task, is an end like any other.
`mc gate tests/mc/run-session.test.js tests/mc/run-plan.test.js`, then `mc gate`, `mc publish`, `mc merge memoro-cli <pr>`.

steps.title: A branch behind its merged pull request's head, with the remote gone, has landed
steps.done_when: `landedThroughRemote` in `src/mc/branch-landed.js` reads the merged pull request's `headRefOid` itself (fetching `refs/pull/<n>/head` when the object is missing) instead of requiring `origin/<branch>`; the new tests in `tests/mc/branch-landed.test.js` and `tests/mc/run.test.js` pass; `mc gate` is green.
instruction: Why: on 2026-10-18 at 00:25Z `sql-schema-drift` step 3 was started on `sql-schema-drift-3`, the branch memoro #13762 had merged from at 2026-10-17 22:04Z (runner.log: `merge conflict in: docs/plans/sql/operating-budgets-baseline.json`, and no `has already landed — moved to` line). Its session had to leave the branch by hand (#13779 on `sql-schema-drift-sd3`) after `mc publish` refused the push. #938 added `landedThroughRemote` for a branch the merger restacked, and it did not cover this one. The workarea's tip was `932ea680`, step 2's own commit. #13762's head on GitHub is `e55b07e3` because the merger's mend session pushed `b7ca58ee` (main merged in) and `e55b07e3` onto the branch after the step session ended. So the tip is an ancestor of the merged head and is not equal to it.

All three checks in `freshBranch` (`src/mc/run.js`, near line 1147) said no. (1) `branchLanded`: main has the mend's version of the baseline file, so the merge conflicts and the answer is `unknown`. (2) `mergedAtTip`: the merged head `e55b07e3` is not the tip `932ea680`. (3) `landedThroughRemote` (`src/mc/branch-landed.js`): it requires `git rev-parse origin/<branch>` to equal the merged head, but GitHub deleted the head branch after the merge, and memoro's checkout has `fetch.prune=true`. The `git fetch -q origin` that opens `freshBranch` therefore removed `origin/sql-schema-drift-3`, the rev-parse failed, and the answer was null. GitHub keeps every pull request's head as `refs/pull/<n>/head` after the branch is deleted, so the merged head can be read from GitHub's answer, not from the remote branch.

Fix, in `landedThroughRemote` in `src/mc/branch-landed.js`. Keep the `gh pr list --head <branch> --state merged` call and the newest-by-`mergedAt` pick as they are. Then replace the two lines that read `origin/<branch>` and compare it with these: `const head = newest.headRefOid; if (!head) return null;`. When `git(['cat-file', '-e', `${head}^{commit}`]) === null`, run `git(['fetch', '-q', 'origin', `refs/pull/${newest.number}/head`])` and ask `cat-file -e` again. If it is still null, return null. The `rev-list --no-merges --cherry-pick --right-only` line and the `merge-base --is-ancestor <sha> origin/main` loop stay as they are, with `head` in place of `newest.headRefOid`. A local branch at or behind the merged head now reads as landed. A branch that carries a commit of its own that neither the head nor origin/main has still returns null. Rewrite the function's doc comment to say this. Name the 2026-10-18 case (`sql-schema-drift-3`, #13762: the mend pushed after the step, and the deleted branch was pruned by the fetch). Rewrite the `freshBranch` doc comment's last paragraph in `src/mc/run.js` the same way. `freshBranch` itself does not change: it already asks `landedRemotely` on both `unknown` and `ahead`.

Tests in `tests/mc/branch-landed.test.js`, inside `describe('landedThroughRemote')`. Add a fixture `mended({ fetched = false, pullRef = true } = {})` next to `restacked()` and build it the same way: a bare origin, and `repo` on `feat` with commit A pushed. A second clone `other` (`git clone -q <origin> other`, `switch feat`) commits B and pushes `feat`. When `pullRef` is set it also pushes `B:refs/pull/13762/head`. When `fetched` is set, `repo` runs `git fetch -q origin` at that point. Then `other` runs `git push -q origin --delete feat`, and `repo` runs `git fetch -q --prune origin`. Return `{ root, repo, head: <sha of B>, cleanup }`. Cases: (1) `mended({ fetched: true })`: `rev-parse --verify origin/feat` fails, and `landedThroughRemote(fx.repo, 'feat', { gh: pulls(fx.head) })` deep-equals `{ number: 13762, merged_at: … }`. Change `pulls` to take the number, or add a second helper, so the answer carries `number: 13762`. (2) `mended()`: B is not local at first (`cat-file -e` fails before the call), the result is the same, and afterwards `cat-file -e <B>` succeeds. (3) `mended({ pullRef: false })`: null. (4) `mended({ fetched: true })` plus a local commit C on `feat`: null. Rename the existing test 'is null when origin/<branch> is not the merged pull request\'s head' to 'is null when the local branch carries a commit neither the merged head nor origin/main has'. Its body still passes unchanged.

Tests in `tests/mc/run.test.js`. In `fixture` (line 29), add two options: `revList = {}` and `notInMain = []`. In its `git` stub, before the `merge-base` line (~321), add: `if (args[0] === 'merge-base' && args[1] === '--is-ancestor' && notInMain.includes(args[2])) return { ok: false, stdout: '' };` and `if (args[0] === 'rev-list') { const range = args.find((a) => a.includes('...')); if (range in revList) return { ok: true, stdout: revList[range] }; }`. The test 'a conflicting branch with a commit after its merged pull request is left where it is' (~line 879) now needs `revList: { 'aaa111...beta': 'bbb222' }, notInMain: ['bbb222']`, because the remote branch no longer stands in for that answer. Add a test after it: 'a branch behind its merged pull request\'s head, whose remote branch is gone, is moved to `<name>-<n>` from origin/main'. Use `conflicted: ['beta']`, `refs: { beta: ['beta', 'beta-2'] }`, `tips: { beta: '932ea680' }`, `merged: { beta: [{ number: 13762, mergedAt: '2026-10-17T22:04:34Z', headRefOid: 'e55b07e3' }] }`, `session: okSession()` and `gh: { beta: { number: 88, title: 'Beta step' } }`. Assert that `f.calls.checkouts` deep-equals `[['/w/beta/memoro', 'beta-3']]`, that a git call includes `rev-list` and `e55b07e3...beta`, and that runner.log matches `/beta: beta has already landed — moved to beta-3 from origin\/main/u`. The existing restack test (~line 861) must pass unchanged.

In `docs/technical/mc-run.md` § step 8 *The branch* (~line 422), add one sentence after the `mergedAtTip` sentence. It says that a branch whose tip is at or behind the newest merged pull request's head counts as landed, with nothing of its own beyond that head and origin/main. The head is read from GitHub and fetched as `refs/pull/<n>/head` when it is missing locally, because the remote branch is deleted on merge and pruned by the fetch (`sql-schema-drift-3`, 2026-10-18).
`mc gate tests/mc/branch-landed.test.js tests/mc/run.test.js`, then `mc gate`, `mc publish`, `mc merge memoro-cli <pr>`.

steps.title: The runner does not hand out a step that has landed
steps.done_when: `queue()` in `src/mc/run.js` writes `done` on a `ready` or `failed` step whose register entry carries `landed`, before any pick, and says so in runner.log; the new tests in `tests/mc/run.test.js` pass; `mc gate` is green.
instruction: Why: `log-page` step 1 landed as memoro #13590 (merger.log 2026-10-12T06:28:21Z: `log-page step 1 is done`, written by `landedPatch` in `src/mc/merge-step.js`, which sets `status: 'done'` together with `landed: { sha, into, at }`). Later that day the register showed the step `ready` again. The runner started it twice, at 18:36Z and 20:24Z. Both sessions found the work already on main and ended without a pull request (`step 1 failed — the session ended success (rc 0) with no pull request`), and step 2, which was ready, waited behind it until a person ran `mc step done log-page 1 --pr 13590`. Whatever moved the status, `patchStep` (`src/mc/register.js`) keeps every field a patch does not name, so the `landed` record stays on the step. The picker never reads `landed`. `planState` (`src/mc/plan-schema.js`) and `chooseKind` (`src/mc/run-plan.js`) look only at `status`.

Fix, in `src/mc/run.js`. Add `function sweepLanded(plans)` beside `sweepLanding` (~line 844), shaped like it. For each record, walk `record.plan.steps`. When a step's `status` is `ready` or `failed`, read the register entry (`readEntry(root, record.project, { read: deps.read })`). If `entry.steps[index].landed` is non-null, write `recordStep(record.project, index, { status: 'done', reason: null, comment })` and lay the written entry over the record with `applyEntry`, the way `sweepLanding` does. The comment is `Set done by the runner on ${stamp()}: it landed as ${sha7} into ${into} on ${at}; a landed step is not run again.`, where `sha7` is `String(landed.sha || '?').slice(0, 7)`, `into` is `landed.into || 'main'` and `at` is `landed.at || 'an unknown time'`. Then `say(`${record.project}: step ${index + 1} landed as ${sha7} into ${into} but stood ${status} — done, not handed out again`)`. Leave `running`, `landing`, `blocked` and `done` steps alone. A `running` step whose session is gone has already been made `ready` by `sweepRunning`, which runs first. Wire it into `queue()` at line ~2833: `plans.push(...sweepLanded(sweepLanding(sweepRunning(overlayPlans(…)))))`, and extend the comment above that line by one clause for it. `runStepClaimed` re-reads the register for its own choice (`standing`, ~line 2326), so it sees the `done` that was written here. Nothing else changes.

Tests in `tests/mc/run.test.js`, next to 'the step after a landing one starts at once, on a branch on top of it', using `twoSteps` and seeding `f.files['/w/runner/projects/m.json']` the way that test does (keys `S1`, `S2`, `S3`). (1) S1 is `{ key: 'S1', status: 'ready', pr: null, branch: 'm-3', comments: [], attempts: 0, landed: { sha: '583009b1aa', into: 'main', at: '2026-10-12T06:28:21Z' } }` and S2 and S3 are plain `ready`, with `session: okSession()`. After `await createRunner({ deps: f.deps }).pass()`, `f.calls.sessions[0].env.MC_STEP` is `'m:1'`, `registerOf(f, 'm').steps[0].status` is `'done'`, its last comment starts with `Set done by the runner on`, and runner.log matches `/m: step 1 landed as 583009b into main but stood ready — done, not handed out again/u`. (2) The same with S1 `status: 'failed', reason: 'the session ended success (rc 0) with no pull request'`: same assertions, with `stood failed`. (3) Control: S1 `ready` with no `landed`: the session's `MC_STEP` is `'m:0'` and S1 is not `done` before the session runs. Assert this through the session's `MC_STEP` only.

In `docs/technical/mc-run.md`, where the picker's sweeps are described (search for `sweepLanding`, or add the line under *The register*), add one sentence. A `ready` or `failed` step whose register entry carries `landed` is written `done` before the pick and said in runner.log (`log-page` step 1, 2026-10-12).
`mc gate tests/mc/run.test.js`, then `mc gate`, `mc publish`, `mc merge memoro-cli <pr>`.

steps.title: mc step ready refuses a step that has landed
steps.done_when: `mc step ready <project> <n>` exits 1 without writing when the step's register entry carries `landed`, and names `mc step done`; the new test in `tests/mc/commands/step.test.js` passes; `mc gate` is green.
instruction: Why: `mc step ready` (`src/mc/commands/step.js`, the `if (status === 'ready')` block near line 121) sets `pr: null` and `status: 'ready'` on any step, including one whose pull request has merged. `patchStep` keeps `landed`, so the register then holds a landed step the runner would run again. This is one way a landed step gets back to `ready`, the state `log-page` step 1 was in on 2026-10-12. The runner now writes such a step `done` (the step before this one), but the person who typed the command should be told at the time, not by a runner.log line ten minutes later.

Fix: as the first thing inside `if (status === 'ready') {`, before the open-PR check, add: `if (step.landed) { const sha7 = String(step.landed.sha || '?').slice(0, 7); stderr.write(`mc: ${target.project} step ${index + 1} landed as ${sha7} into ${step.landed.into || 'main'}${step.landed.at ? ` on ${step.landed.at}` : ''} — it is done, not ready: mc step done ${target.project} ${index + 1}. Work it left undone is a new step in the plan.\n`); return 1; }`. Add one line to the file's top comment, under the existing `ready` paragraph, saying a landed step is refused. Nothing else changes.

Test in `tests/mc/commands/step.test.js`, after 'ready stays blocked when the placeholder could not be closed'. Call `const f = fixture();`, then `f.deps.write(registerPath(ROOT, 'p'), { project: 'p', repo: 'memoro', steps: [{ key: 'A', status: 'failed', pr: null, reason: 'no pull request', landed: { sha: '583009b1aa', into: 'main', at: '2026-10-12T06:28:21Z' } }, { key: 'B', status: 'ready' }] })`. `await run(['ready', 'p', '1'], f.deps)` returns 1. `f.err.join('')` matches `/p step 1 landed as 583009b into main on 2026-10-12T06:28:21Z — it is done, not ready: mc step done p 1/u`. `f.step(0).status` is still `'failed'`. A second assertion in the same test: `run(['ready', 'p', '2'], f.deps)` returns 0, because a step with no `landed` is unaffected.
`mc gate tests/mc/commands/step.test.js`, then `mc gate`, `mc publish`, `mc merge memoro-cli <pr>`.

steps.title: A lane file whose pid is dead is swept by the runner and left out of the drain
steps.done_when: `stepsHeld` in `src/mc/run.js` moves a `current-*.json` naming a dead pid to `runner/log/dead-<file>-<pid>.json` with one line, `drainState` in `src/mc/run-control.js` leaves such a file out of `inFlight`, the new tests in `tests/mc/run.test.js` and `tests/mc/run-control.test.js` pass, and `mc gate` is green.
instruction: Why: on 2026-10-18 `~/mc/runner/current-memoro-2.json` named `msr-core-residue` step 4 under runner pid 41100, which had been gone for 19 hours. A lane removes its file in the `finally` of the step it runs (`runStep`, `src/mc/run.js` around line 2463), and a killed runner never reaches that `finally`. Nothing removes the file afterwards: `stepsHeld()` (`src/mc/run.js` around line 2936) already treats a dead pid as nobody's (`other` is false) but leaves the file, and `drainState` (`src/mc/run-control.js` around line 603) lists every `current-*.json` without asking whether its pid is alive, so `drainWaiting` / `drainLine` / `stopLine` name a step nobody runs (`mc run --update` printed `waiting on … msr-core-residue step 4 (memoro#3, 19 h)`). The page's `stale:` line (`nowBlock`, `src/mc/status-collect.js` around line 280) already tests `alive` and is a pure reader; it is not changed and its stale line disappears once the runner has swept the file.

Fix 1, the sweep, in `createRunner` in `src/mc/run.js`. Add `basename` to the `node:path` import (line 107). In `stepsHeld()`, after parsing each file: when `known && owner !== pid && !alive(owner)`, the file is a dead runner's. Move it with `deps.move(path, join(paths.log, `dead-${basename(path, '.json')}-${owner}.json`))` (the real `deps.move` makes the directory and returns a boolean, `src/mc/run.js` around line 466; a missing `deps.move` or a `false` return falls back to `remove(path)`), say one line, and leave that entry out of the array `stepsHeld` returns. The line, exactly: `say(`lane file ${basename(path)} names pid ${owner}, which is gone — ${held?.name || 'no step'}${Number.isInteger(held?.step) ? ` step ${held.step}` : ''}; moved to log/${basename(to)}`)` where `to` is the destination path. A file with no integer pid (unparseable, or `{}`) is left exactly as today: not moved, `pid: null`, `other: false`. This process's own files (`owner === pid`) are never moved. Because `stepsHeld` is what `nextStep`, `laneHolder`, `stillHeld` and `clearRunner` all read, every one of them now sweeps; the sweep is synchronous and touches only dead pids, so it cannot race a live lane's own `finally`. Update the doc comment above `stepsHeld` to say a file naming a dead pid is moved to `runner/log/` and said, not returned.

Do not touch `sweepRunning` (`src/mc/run.js` around line 816): it interrupts the register's `running` step from the register's own `session.pid`, never from the lane file, so moving the lane file does not change what it records.

Fix 2, the drain, in `src/mc/run-control.js`. `drainState({ paths, read, list, now, lanes = null, alive = pidAlive })` (`pidAlive` is already imported from `./status-collect.js`, line 62). In the `inFlight` map, a file whose parsed `current.pid` is an integer and `!alive(current.pid)` is dropped: change the chain to map to the entry or `null` and `.filter(Boolean)`. A file with no integer pid stays in `inFlight` as today (the existing test 'drainLine: nothing in flight, a first lane, and no UPDATE at all' relies on that). Add one sentence to the doc comment above `drainState`: a file whose runner pid is gone is not a step in flight. Pass `alive: deps.alive` in every `drainState` call in this file: `stepsOf` (around line 455), `progressLines` (around 463), `stopRunner` (around 515) and `requestUpdate`'s `state` (around 718). In `src/mc/run.js`, the `drainTick` call (around line 3409) passes `alive: isAlive` (defined in `runLoop` around line 3239).

Tests in `tests/mc/run.test.js`, beside 'runLoop: a runner.json naming a pid that is gone is cleared, not a wall' (around line 1908), using `fixture` (runner pid 4242, `livePids` the pids `alive` answers true for, `calls.moved` records each move): (1) 'a lane file naming a dead pid is moved to runner/log and said once': `const f = fixture({ plans: { memoro: {} }, session: okSession(), livePids: [7000] })`; `f.files['/w/runner/current-memoro-2.json'] = JSON.stringify({ name: 'msr-core-residue', step: 4, pid: 41100, lane: 2 })` and `f.files['/w/runner/current-memoro-1.json'] = JSON.stringify({ name: 'a', step: 1, pid: 7000, lane: 1 })`; `const runner = createRunner({ deps: f.deps })`; `runner.stepsHeld()` returns exactly one entry, pid 7000 with `other: true`; `'/w/runner/current-memoro-2.json' in f.files` is false; `f.files['/w/runner/log/dead-current-memoro-2-41100.json']` is the old text; `f.calls.moved` contains `['/w/runner/current-memoro-2.json', '/w/runner/log/dead-current-memoro-2-41100.json']`; runner.log matches `/lane file current-memoro-2\.json names pid 41100, which is gone — msr-core-residue step 4; moved to log\/dead-current-memoro-2-41100\.json/u`; a second `runner.stepsHeld()` adds no second such line. (2) 'a lane file with no pid is not swept': `f.files['/w/runner/current-memoro.json'] = '{}'`, `runner.stepsHeld()` returns one entry with `pid: null`, the file is still there and `f.calls.moved` is empty.

Tests in `tests/mc/run-control.test.js`, beside 'drainLine: nothing in flight, a first lane, and no UPDATE at all' (around line 564), with that file's `fixture` (`live` is the pids `deps.alive` answers true for): 'drainState leaves out a lane whose runner pid is gone': `fixture({ live: [100], files: { [paths.update]: '2026-08-30T17:50:00Z\n', [`${paths.dir}/current-memoro-2.json`]: JSON.stringify({ name: 'msr-core-residue', step: 4, pid: 41100, started: '2026-08-29T13:39:13Z' }), [`${paths.dir}/current-memoro-cli.json`]: JSON.stringify({ name: 'mc-ui', step: 1, pid: 100, started: '2026-08-30T17:58:00Z' }) } })`; `drainState({ paths, read, list, now, alive: fx.deps.alive })` has `inFlight.map((s) => s.name)` equal to `['mc-ui']`, and `drainLine(state)` does not match `/msr-core-residue/u`.

Then run `node --test --import ./tests/_isolate-home.mjs tests/mc/run.test.js tests/mc/run-control.test.js`. If an existing test now fails because its fixture's lane file names a pid the fixture does not list as live while the test means that runner to be alive, add the pid to that fixture's `livePids` / `live`; change no assertion. Docs: in `docs/technical/mc-run.md`, the `current-<repo>.json` bullet (around line 1218) gains one sentence: a file whose runner pid is gone is moved to `runner/log/dead-<file>-<pid>.json` by the next runner that reads it, and the drain and stop lines leave it out.
`mc gate tests/mc/run.test.js`, `mc gate tests/mc/run-control.test.js`, then `mc gate`, `mc publish`, `mc merge memoro-cli <pr>`.

steps.title: The total lane cap is read live and counts every live runner's steps
steps.done_when: `takeSlot` in `src/mc/run.js` reads `total` from `lanes.json` on every call and counts this process's slots plus the lane files of other live runners, `createRunner` takes no `total`, `mc run lanes` says the total applies now, the new and changed tests in `tests/mc/run.test.js` and `tests/mc/commands/run-lanes.test.js` pass, and `mc gate` is green.
instruction: Why: on 2026-10-10 `mc run lanes 5 --total 6` left the running runner at `6 per repository, 8 in total`, seven steps ran under a cap of six, and load reached 65 on 8 cores. Two causes, both in `src/mc/run.js`. (a) `runLoop` reads `lanes.json` once (`const laneSetting = (deps.laneCount || readLaneCount)()`, around line 3225) and hands `total` to `createRunner`, which fixes `cap` for the life of the process (around line 2087). (b) `takeSlot` (around line 2089) compares only this process's `running`: after a handover (ruling 28) the predecessor is still finishing its steps while the successor starts up to `total` new ones, so two runners hold up to twice the cap. This step depends on step 1: `stepsHeld()` no longer returns a dead pid's file, so a dead runner's leftovers are never counted.

Fix in `createRunner` (`src/mc/run.js`): remove the `total = null` parameter and its comment (around lines 587–590). Replace `const cap = …` and `takeSlot` (around lines 2086–2093) with: `let running = 0; let seen = { held: 0, cap: null };` a function `capNow()` returning `(deps.laneCount || readLaneCount)()?.total` when it is an integer above 0, else `null`; and `function takeSlot() { const cap = capNow(); const held = cap === null ? running : running + stepsHeld().filter((h) => h.other).length; seen = { held, cap }; if (cap !== null && held >= cap) return false; running += 1; return true; }`. `stepsHeld` is a function declaration in the same scope, so calling it here is fine; it reads files synchronously, so there is still no await between the test and the take. Own steps are counted by `running`, never by their files (a lane's file is written after its slot is taken, which is why the in-process count stays); other live runners' steps are counted by their files, because they take no new step after a handover (`holdUpdate`) and their count only falls. In `waitForSlot` (around line 2108) the line becomes `say(`${name}: ${seen.held} of ${seen.cap} steps in flight on this machine — waiting for a lane`)`; the poll loop is unchanged, and since every poll calls `takeSlot`, a raised total lets a waiting lane go within `TOTAL_POLL_MS` and a lowered one holds the next start at once. Rewrite the doc comment above `running` (around lines 2053–2084): the total is read from `lanes.json` each time a slot is taken, and the count is this process's claims plus the steps other live runners hold by their lane files (a predecessor finishing after a handover); keep its paragraphs on why the own count is a claim and on the unordered waiters.

In `runLoop` (around lines 3220–3226): `createRunner({ merge, deps })`, and the comment above says `per_repo` is read once at start (it is how many lane loops exist) while `total` is read by `takeSlot` each time a slot is taken. `laneSetting` stays for `per_repo` and for the `lanes: … per repository, … in total` start line (around line 3366), which is unchanged.

The verb, in `lanes` in `src/mc/commands/run.js` (around lines 145–152): the first line becomes `lanes ${phrase(pair, repos)} — the total applies now, per repository from the next start`, and the last line becomes `a running runner takes the total at its next start of a step; a new per-repository count takes mc run --update, after the step it is in`. In `src/mc/lane-count.js`, the header comment's sentence 'The runner reads them once, at start — a running runner keeps what it was started with, and `mc run --update` (or stop and start) is how a new value takes effect' becomes: `per_repo` is read once, at start, and takes effect with `mc run --update`; `total` is read each time a step is about to start, so it applies at once. In `docs/technical/mc-run.md`, the paragraph around line 1041 ('`total` as an in-process claim each lane takes…') says the same two facts: read live at each `takeSlot`, and counted as this process's claims plus the lane files of other live runners.

Tests in `tests/mc/run.test.js`, section 'the total lane cap' (around line 3602). First, the two tests that call `createRunner({ deps: f.deps, total: 1 })` (around lines 3691 and 3719) become `f.deps.laneCount = () => ({ per_repo: 1, total: 1 }); const runner = createRunner({ deps: f.deps });` with no other change. Then add, using the same pattern as 'a lane held back by the total goes through when the slot frees' (blocking session, `release`, `turns`, `f.deps.sleep = () => new Promise((resolve) => { setImmediate(resolve); })`): (1) 'a total changed while the runner runs applies to the next slot': `let total = 2; f.deps.laneCount = () => ({ per_repo: 1, total });` plans `{ memoro: { a: ready, b: ready } }`; start `runStep('a', world, { lane: 0 })`, `await turns(4)`, set `total = 1`, start `runStep('b', world, { lane: 1 })`, `await turns()`; `starts` is `['a']` and runner.log matches `/b: 1 of 1 steps in flight on this machine — waiting for a lane/u`; set `total = 2`, `await turns()`; `starts` is `['a', 'b']`; `release()` and both resolve to `'ran'`. (2) 'a live predecessor\'s steps count against the total': `fixture({ plans: { memoro: { a: ready } }, session: okSession(), livePids: [7000] })`, `f.files['/w/runner/current-memoro-cli.json'] = JSON.stringify({ name: 'z', step: 1, pid: 7000, lane: 0 })`, `f.deps.laneCount = () => ({ per_repo: 1, total: 1 })`; `const a = runner.runStep('a', world, { lane: 0 })`, `await turns()`; no session started and runner.log matches `/a: 1 of 1 steps in flight on this machine — waiting for a lane/u`; `delete f.files['/w/runner/current-memoro-cli.json']`, `await turns()`; `f.calls.sessions.length` is 1 (the session here is `okSession()`, which does not block) and `a` resolves to `'ran'`; before the delete, `f.calls.sessions.length` is 0. (3) 'a dead runner\'s lane file does not count': the same with `livePids: []` and pid 7001; the session starts without waiting and runner.log does not match `/waiting for a lane/u`.

Tests in `tests/mc/commands/run-lanes.test.js` (around lines 84–97): the four expected first lines end in ` — the total applies now, per repository from the next start` instead of ` from the next start`, and the regex on `per.out.at(-1)` becomes `/a running runner takes the total at its next start of a step; a new per-repository count takes mc run --update, after the step it is in/u`.
`mc gate tests/mc/run.test.js`, `mc gate tests/mc/commands/run-lanes.test.js`, then `mc gate`, `mc publish`, `mc merge memoro-cli <pr>`.

steps.title: mc hook pre-tool applies the repositories' own PreToolUse hooks when the session started outside them
steps.done_when: `repoHookDecision` in `src/mc/hooks.js` runs each worktree's `.claude/settings.json` PreToolUse hooks and `mc hook pre-tool` denies with their reason before its own rules; the new tests in `tests/mc/hooks.test.js` pass; `mc gate` is green.
instruction: Why: a plan session starts in `~/mc/plan/<programme>/` (`src/mc/commands/plan.js`, `openInWorkArea` with `areaRoot: ready.path`, `is_git: false`), the parent of the checkouts. Claude Code loads project hooks only from the start directory's `.claude/settings.json`, so memoro's PreToolUse hooks (`.claude/hooks/block-prod-wrangler.sh`, `block-sqlite-state.sh`, `block-shared-stash.sh`, all on matcher `Bash`; `block-sqlite-state.sh` also on `Read`) never load there. On 2026-10-12 a plan session ran `npx wrangler d1 execute memoro-db --remote` several times and `wrangler secret list` unblocked, and phone numbers and user ids from `sms_messages` reached its context. Today `mc hook session-start` only warns (`sessionStartContext` in `src/mc/hooks.js` line 153).

Choice: mc's own PreToolUse hook, already registered globally in `~/.claude/settings.json` as `mc hook pre-tool 2>/dev/null || true` on matcher `Bash|Write`, runs the repositories' hooks itself. It already acts only on mc's ground (`inMcTerritory`) and already finds a workarea's worktrees (`worktreesAt`), and it reads each repository's `.claude/settings.json` live, so nothing is copied and nothing drifts when memoro changes its hooks. Not `--settings` on the plan launch: it covers only sessions `mc plan` starts with claude, and `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` in memoro's hook commands would point at the plan directory, so every path would have to be rewritten into a generated file that goes stale. Not the global settings: the hooks would fire in every directory with `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` naming the wrong repository, and a copy drifts. memoro's three blocking scripts all answer with `hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision: "deny"` JSON on stdout and exit 0, which is exactly what mc's hook already prints, so their answer can be passed through.

In `src/mc/hooks.js` add `readFileSync` to the `node:fs` import and add two exported functions after `preToolDecision`. (1) `repoPreToolHooks(worktree, tool, { readFileSync: read = readFileSync } = {})`: read `join(worktree, '.claude', 'settings.json')`, `JSON.parse` it; on any throw return `[]`. From `settings.hooks?.PreToolUse` (not an array → `[]`) keep each entry whose `matcher` is absent, `''` or `'*'`, or for which `new RegExp(`^(?:${matcher})$`, 'u').test(tool)` is true (a matcher that will not compile matches nothing); return the `command` strings of its `hooks` whose `type` is `'command'` and whose `command` is a non-empty string, in file order. (2) `repoHookDecision(input, { cwd, projectDir = null, worktreesAt: find = worktreesAt, readFileSync: read = readFileSync, spawnSync: spawn = spawnSync, env = process.env, findDeps = {} } = {})`: `tool = input?.tool_name`; no tool → `null`. `const { worktrees } = find(cwd, findDeps)`. Skip a worktree whose `resolve(worktree)` equals `resolve(projectDir)` when `projectDir` is set: Claude Code already loaded that one's settings itself. For each remaining worktree in order, for each command from `repoPreToolHooks(entry.worktree, tool, { readFileSync: read })`: `const r = spawn('/bin/sh', ['-c', command], { cwd: entry.worktree, input: JSON.stringify(input), encoding: 'utf8', timeout: 10_000, env: { ...env, CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR: entry.worktree } })`. If `r.status === 2` return `{ id: 'repo-hook', reason: `${entry.name} hook: ${String(r.stderr || '').trim() || command}` }` (Claude Code's own meaning of exit 2). Otherwise try `JSON.parse(String(r.stdout || '').trim())`; when `parsed?.hookSpecificOutput?.permissionDecision === 'deny'` return `{ id: 'repo-hook', reason: `${entry.name} hook: ${parsed.hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecisionReason || command}` }`. Anything else — empty stdout, unparseable stdout, a nonzero exit other than 2, a timeout (`r.error`), `allow` or `ask` — is not a denial: go on to the next command. Return `null` when nothing denied. Above the two functions, a short comment: a session that started outside a repository (a plan directory, a workarea) never loaded that repository's hooks, and memoro's are its data-access policy, so mc runs them; `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` is the worktree so their `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.claude/hooks/...` paths resolve.

In `src/mc/commands/hook.js`, `pre-tool` branch, after the `inMcTerritory` check and before `preToolDecision`: `const borrowed = (deps.repoHookDecision || repoHookDecision)(input, { cwd, projectDir: (deps.env || process.env).CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR || null });` and then `const decision = borrowed || preToolDecision(...)` (the existing call unchanged). The repository's denial comes first: a safety block outranks a turn to an mc verb. The JSON written is unchanged, so the reason reads `mc: memoro hook: Blocked by .claude/hooks/block-prod-wrangler.sh: …`. Import `repoHookDecision` beside the other names from `../hooks.js`. Update the file's header comment and `usage()` to say pre-tool also runs the PreToolUse hooks of every worktree the session did not start in.

steps.title: The mc digest does not count a landed merge or a pushed mend as a failure
steps.done_when: `cliRows` in `src/mc/helper-cli-collect.js` skips runs.tsv rows whose note is exactly `merged` or `pushed` with exit 0; the new test in `tests/mc/helper-cli-collect.test.js` passes; `mc gate` is green.
instruction: Why: the 2026-10-18 digest listed 38 new fingerprints, nearly all landings that worked. In `cliRows` (`src/mc/helper-cli-collect.js`, the runs.tsv loop, line 184) a row is skipped as normal only when its note matches `/success/` with exit 0 or 143. A `merge` row that landed is written with note `merged` (`src/mc/merger.js` line 605: `landed ? 'merged' : `red,${…}``) and a `mend` that pushed with note `pushed` (`src/mc/mend.js` line 280). Neither matches, so every landing is bumped as `runner step: merge <project> — merged (exit N)`, and the project name in the fingerprint (`{ name }`, kept deliberately, see `signature`) makes each landing project a new line each day. Measured in `~/mc/runner/log/runs.tsv` today: 563 `merge merged 0` and 52 `mend pushed 0` rows, none with a nonzero exit; every failing merge note starts with `red,` and every failing mend note is `nothing`, `timed-out` or `failed`.

Fix, in `src/mc/helper-cli-collect.js`: add a module constant beside `CLI_ROW_CAP`: `/** A runner row that did its job without saying success: a merge that landed, a mend that pushed. */ export const LANDED_NOTES = new Set(['merged', 'pushed']);`. In the loop, directly after line 184 (the `/success/` skip), add `if (LANDED_NOTES.has(outcome) && code === '0') continue;` with a one-line comment: `merger.js` and `mend.js` write these notes for a landing, so they are normal; a nonzero exit with the same note is still a finding. The match is on the whole note, so `red,merge` and `success,failed` are unaffected. The fingerprint (`{ name: cell[name] }`) is unchanged.

Test in `tests/mc/helper-cli-collect.test.js`, a new `it('a merge that landed and a mend that pushed are not findings', …)` inside `describe('the four sources')`, after 'a successful step the runner grace-killed is not a finding' (around line 148), using `ground()`, `runs()` and `collect()` as that test does. Rows (13 tab-separated cells, as the existing rows): `'2026-08-30T09:00:00Z\tzeta\tmerge\t0\t100\t7\t-\t-\t-\t-\t-\t-\tmerged'`, `'2026-08-30T09:10:00Z\teta\tmend\t0\t100\t7\t-\t-\t-\t-\t-\t-\tpushed'`, `'2026-08-30T09:20:00Z\ttheta\tmerge\t1\t100\t7\t-\t-\t-\t-\t-\t-\tred,red'`, `'2026-08-30T09:30:00Z\tiota\tmerge\t1\t100\t7\t-\t-\t-\t-\t-\t-\tmerged'`, `'2026-08-30T09:40:00Z\tkappa\tmend\t1\t100\t7\t-\t-\t-\t-\t-\t-\tnothing'`. Assert on `collect(g).rows.map((r) => r.message)`: no message matches `/zeta/u` ('a landed merge is not a finding') or `/\beta\b/u` ('a pushed mend is not a finding'); one matches `/theta.*red,red.*exit N/u`, one `/iota.*merged.*exit N/u` ('merged with a nonzero exit is still a finding'), one `/kappa.*nothing.*exit N/u`. `finally { g.cleanup(); }`.

`mc gate tests/mc/helper-cli-collect.test.js`, then `mc gate`, `mc publish`, `mc merge memoro-cli <pr>`. This is the plan's last step: in the same PR set every `success_criteria[].met` in this plan to true.
